test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If the radius of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 40% and its height is increased by 75%, its volume will be decreased by:
solution:
**Given:**

Initial radius of the cylinder = r

Initial height of the cylinder = h

Initial volume of the cylinder = V = πr²h

New radius = 60% of r = 0.6r

New height = 175% of h = 1.75h

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cylinder = πr²h

Percentage change in volume = [(Initial Volume - New Volume) / Initial Volume] × 100

**Calculation:**

New Volume (V') = π(New radius)²(New height)

⇒ V' = π(0.6r)²(1.75h)

⇒ V' = π(0.36r²)(1.75h)

⇒ V' = π(0.63r²h)

New Volume = 63% of the Initial Volume

Percentage decrease in volume = 100% - 63%

⇒ Percentage decrease = 37%

**The volume will be decreased by 37%.**
